name: Wittig reaction of anisaldehyde with a stabilized ylide: the two transition structures weighted by their free energies

reference.citation: Z. Chen, Y. Nieves-Quinones, J. R. Waas, D. A. Singleton, J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2014, 136, 13122-13125
reference.method: 13C KIEs at natural abundance by NMR at 67 C: anisaldehyde recovered from two reactions taken to 69 +/- 2% and 73 +/- 2% conversion (standard: the carbons meta to the aldehyde); the ylide carbons from product at 20% conversion of the ylide against complete conversion (standard: the ketone methyl carbon); values from Figure 1, predictions from Table 1 and SI Table S4, free energies from Figure 2, structures from the SI

reference.citation: H. J. A. Dale, A. G. Leach, G. C. Lloyd-Jones, J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2021, 143, 21079-21099 (Case Study III)
reference.method: the same data as an example of commitment between transition structures in series

notes: The same jobs and labels as wittig_anisaldehyde, with the steps weighted by the harmonic free energies of 4-TS and 6-TS, 25.9 and 26.0 kcal/mol (Figure 2), as for a betaine in equilibrium with the starting materials. Kinisot weights each step by its rate including Bell tunnelling, so C_f = 0.822 rather than exp[(G_4 - G_6)/RT] = 0.862, which would give KIEs 3e-4 higher. The absolute KIEs are 1.0276 and 1.0069 (Table 1: 1.028 and 1.008; the paper's own single-structure values give 1.0070 for the ylide CH carbon). The paper rejects this weighting: experiment agrees with the trajectories, most of which pass the betaine without equilibrating. Left out of the overall mean absolute deviation.
level_of_theory: M06-2X/6-31+G(d,p), PCM (THF), Gaussian 16 C.01 frequency jobs at the SI geometries

kies.note: no prediction in the paper; SI Table S4: 4-TS 0.998, 6-TS 0.999
